answer: A falcon does not trust a flock by counting wings; it watches how birds fly together, and an agent economy can do the same. Require every newcomer to forge its identity in public work, stamping each completed task onto the ledger before it can earn anything. Each agent then sits at a vertex in a web of these stamps, and a vertex that only ever vouches for its own neighbors looks suspicious. Random falcon patrols, peers chosen by lottery, swoop in to re-check one stamped task; if two identities share the same vertex trail, both are unmade and their stakes fund the patrol that caught them.
